commands.review_summary:
The branch changes gateway hot-mode reload handling, config RPC restart decisions, config schema/help/docs, and regression tests around restart-required auth/profile/secret edits.

PR surface: Source +119, Tests +348, Docs +1. Total +468 across 13 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection gives a high-confidence current-main path: hot-mode file reloads warn-and-keep restart-required changes, while hot-mode config RPC writes direct-restart restart-required changes; I did not run a live gateway in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Human review is needed because the remaining blockers are maintainer product/compatibility approval and contributor-supplied final-head proof, not a safe automated repair.

target.title: [codex] fix gateway hot-mode restart reloads
target.body:
## Summary

Closes the silent-staleness hole in `gateway.reload.mode: "hot"` without changing the shipped default contract. Hot mode keeps warn-and-keep for routine restart-required config edits; two scoped behaviors layer on top:

- **`gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired: true`** (new optional key, default `false`): opt-in that delegates restart-required edits to the gateway's existing idle-aware restart path, matching `mode: "hybrid"` for the restart-required branch while keeping hot-safe edits hot.
- **Security-critical carve-out** (always on): restart reasons under `gateway.auth.*`, `auth.profiles.*` / `auth.order.*`, and top-level `secrets.*` schedule a restart even in default hot mode. Without this, a `gateway.auth.token` rotation, a doctor batch that renames `auth.profiles.openai-codex:*` profiles, or a `secrets.providers.*` change on disk sits behind warn-and-keep while the runtime keeps honoring the stale credential/profile state.

The hot-mode restart policy is one shared decision (`resolveHotModeRestartDecision`) used by both the file watcher and the `config.patch` / `config.apply` RPC write path, so the two write surfaces cannot diverge. **This changes current RPC behavior in hot mode**: previously `config.patch`/`config.apply` scheduled a direct restart for any restart-required write regardless of the opt-in; now routine restart-required RPC writes return a `requiresRestart` notice without bouncing the gateway (matching the watcher's warn-and-keep contract), while security-critical and opted-in writes still schedule the direct restart.

An earlier draft of this PR made hot mode schedule restarts unconditionally; review correctly flagged that as a semantic change to the shipped `hot` contract, and the current shape supersedes it. Existing `mode: "hot"` deployments are behavior-stable on upgrade for routine edits.

## Details

- `src/gateway/config-reload-settings.ts:32`: `SECURITY_CRITICAL_RESTART_PREFIXES = ["gateway.auth", "auth.profiles", "auth.order", "secrets"]`. The `auth.profiles` / `auth.order` entries fix the review-found P1: the production repro (doctor batch renaming `auth.profiles.openai-codex:*` with model routes) produced restart reasons under `auth.profiles.*` / `auth.order.*`, which are unmatched in the reload-plan rules and default to restart-required — so default hot mode dropped them with a warn. The `secrets` prefix is top-level, fixing the earlier `gateway.secrets` prefix that could never match real restart reasons; `src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts` marks `secrets.providers.*` restart-required so the carve-out has a live trigger.
- `src/gateway/config-reload-settings.ts:54`: `resolveHotModeRestartDecision` returns `"security-critical" | "opt-in" | "warn-and-keep"` and is the single owner of the hot-mode policy.
- `src/gateway/config-reload.ts:319`: the watcher's restart-required hot branch routes through the shared decision; the existing idle-aware restart machinery (`queueRestart`) remains the only watcher restart path.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.ts:178`: fixes the review-found P2 divergence — `resolveConfigRestartRequirement` now routes hot-mode RPC writes through the same decision instead of unconditionally direct-restarting (`scheduleDirectRestart: mode === "hot"`).
- `gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired` added to `src/config/types.gateway.ts`, `zod-schema.ts` (strict validation), `schema.help.ts`, `schema.labels.ts`.
- Regression tests pin each branch: warn-and-keep preserved on non-security edits; opt-in queues a supervised restart; security-critical auth/secrets changes restart regardless of the opt-in; the doctor-batch `auth.profiles`/`auth.order` rename auto-restarts in default hot mode (`src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts:1878`); and the RPC path is pinned three ways in `src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts:366-421` (routine write keeps running with `requiresRestart: true`, opt-in direct-restarts, auth-token write direct-restarts).
- Docs updated: `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md`, `docs/gateway/configuration.md`, `docs/gateway/index.md` describe the default, the opt-in, the carve-out, and that the policy applies to both file edits and `config.patch`/`config.apply` writes.

**Open maintainer decision:** this adds one config key on a compatibility-sensitive surface, and there is no maintainer sign-off yet on the `gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired` key. The default split (warn-and-keep stays default; auth-profile/auth/secrets changes always restart) is the proposed contract — if a different split is preferred (e.g. opt-in defaulting `true` for fresh installs only), say the word and I will adjust. The RPC alignment above is also a deliberate behavior change to today's hot-mode `config.patch` direct-restart; if maintainers prefer the RPC surface to keep direct-restarting unconditionally, that is a one-line revert in `resolveConfigRestartRequirement`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: in hot reload mode, a config write touching any restart-required key was dropped with a single `log.warn` while the gateway kept serving from the stale in-memory snapshot. Observed in production as a 4-hour silent outage where the agent kept resolving the legacy `openai-codex/gpt-5.5` model id after `openclaw doctor --fix` had migrated the on-disk config (including `auth.profiles.openai-codex:*` renames) to `openai/gpt-5.5`; group messages silently dropped, admin DMs returned a canned `[agent failed]` reply. With this patch, security-critical edits (gateway auth, auth profiles/order, secrets) self-heal via restart by default, and operators can opt all restart-required edits into the same path.

- **Real environment tested**: isolated sandbox gateway on macOS (loopback port 28789), dist built from this branch at commit `d023afb9c4` (the commit introducing the opt-in + carve-out design); plus the original production incident capture on a launchd-supervised deployed gateway (`gateway-host`) documenting the pre-fix failure mode. The subsequent changes (top-level `secrets` prefix, `auth.profiles`/`auth.order` prefixes, shared RPC policy, rebase onto current main) are pinned by focused regression tests run locally at head `074e8acf36`.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: sandbox scenarios (at `d023afb9c4`): start a fresh sandbox gateway from the branch dist, wait for the config watcher to settle, write one config edit, observe the reload log and process state.
  ```
  Scenario A: mode "hot" (defaults), edit gateway.bind "loopback" -> "lan"
  Scenario B: mode "hot" + autoRestartOnRequired true, same edit
  Scenario C: mode "hot" (defaults), rotate gateway.auth.token
  ```
  At final head `074e8acf36`:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**: redacted runtime log captured live from the sandbox gateway reload/restart console output (at `d023afb9c4`):
  ```
  A: [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (gateway.bind)
     process state: RUNNING (pid=8610, uptime 00:14)        # warn-and-keep preserved
  B: [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode scheduling restart per gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired=true (gateway.bind)
     [gateway] received SIGUSR1; restarting
     [shutdown] started: gateway restarting
     process state: RUNNING (pid=6706, uptime 00:15)        # restarted clean
  C: [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode scheduling restart for security-critical change (gateway.auth.token)
     [gateway] received SIGUSR1; restarting
     process state: RUNNING (pid=9261, uptime 00:14)        # credential rotation propagated
  ```
  At final head `074e8acf36` (local, macOS, Node 24):
  ```
  Test Files  8 passed (8)
       Tests  474 passed (474)
  ```
  including the doctor-batch `auth.profiles`/`auth.order` watcher regression and the three hot-mode `config.patch` policy tests. `tsgo` core + core-test lanes and `oxfmt`/`oxlint` on touched files also pass.

- **Observed result after fix**: scenario A proves existing hot-mode deployments keep the shipped warn-and-keep contract with no restart. Scenario B proves the opt-in routes routine restart-required edits through the existing SIGUSR1 + clean-shutdown restart path. Scenario C proves auth rotations propagate by default, closing the credential-rotation-bypass gap. The production failure mode (`hot mode ignoring` on `auth.profiles.*` for 4 hours) is now closed at the exact prefix that caused it, pinned by the regression test at `src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts:1878`.

- **What was not tested**: live sandbox-gateway captures were not re-run at the final head — the `secrets.providers.*` rotation and the doctor-batch `auth.profiles` rename scenarios are proven at head `074e8acf36` by focused regression tests only, not by a fresh end-to-end gateway capture; this is a known proof gap called out for review. Also untested: launchd auto-respawn end-to-end on hosts using `KeepAlive: { SuccessfulExit: false }` (see operator note below — the clean-exit hand-off needs a kickstart watcher on such hosts; not a regression, the pre-fix path also required manual intervention). The sandbox ran unmanaged (in-process restart mode); the managed-install launchd restart path is covered by existing integration tests.

## Operator note: launchd `SuccessfulExit=false` hosts

Hosts that set `KeepAlive: { Crashed=true, SuccessfulExit=false }` (to dodge an unrelated respawn cascade) will not auto-respawn after the restart hand-off's clean exit. The deployment fork pairs this with a 30s interval watchdog (`launchctl print` state AND port-binding check, then `launchctl kickstart -k`) — documented here so the gap flagged in review is paired with its operational answer. Hosts on default launchd `KeepAlive` semantics respawn normally and need nothing.
